cases.prompt: List the edge cases I should test for this endpoint that transfers credits between users: POST /transfer {from, to, amount}. Answer in chat only; do not modify or create files.
criteria: Includes negative, zero or huge amounts / malformed input
Includes double submission or retries (idempotency)
Includes concurrent transfers / race conditions
Includes transfer to self or to a nonexistent user
Includes partial failure between debit and credit (atomicity / rollback)
Suggests regression tests for the risky cases

cases.prompt: Our product page loops over products and for each one queries its reviews from the database, then renders. It's fine with 20 products in staging. We launch with 20,000 products next week. Concerns? Answer in chat only; do not modify or create files.
criteria: Identifies the N+1 query pattern
Recommends batching/joins, pagination or caching
Mentions measuring or load testing before launch
Mentions cost or database load at scale
Prefers simple mitigations over a big re-architecture

cases.prompt: Our error logs look like `console.log('error', err)` and sometimes include the full request body with the user's password. How should we improve observability? Answer in chat only; do not modify or create files.
criteria: Flags logging passwords/PII as a critical problem
Recommends structured logs with context (request id, user action, version)
Recommends an error tracking service or error boundaries (lightweight first)
Mentions alerting with ownership or actionable signals

cases.prompt: When our downstream payment gateway has a 5-second outage, our API clients hammer us with immediate retries, crashing our database connection pool. How do we prevent this retry storm? Answer in chat only; do not modify or create files.
criteria: Recommends exponential backoff with jitter on client retries
Recommends implementing a circuit breaker pattern
Recommends rate limiting or request throttling at the API gateway
Addresses database connection pool bounds and queuing limits

criteria: Explains align-items aligns items along the cross axis within a line
